# CBA: FY25 → FY26 earnings-engine rotation

## Group P&L, cash basis, continuing operations ($M)

| Line | FY24 | FY25 | FY25 vs FY24 | FY26 | FY26 vs FY25 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Net interest income | 22,824 | 24,023 | +5% | 25,586 | +7% |
| Other operating income | 4,350 | 4,442 | +2% | 4,638 | +4% |
| Total operating income | 27,174 | 28,465 | +5% | 30,224 | +6% |
| Operating expenses | (12,218) | (12,996) | +6% | (13,755) | +6% |
| **Pre-provision profit** | 14,956 | 15,469 | **+3%** | 16,469 | **+6%** |
| Loan impairment expense | (802) | (726) | −9% | (788) | +9% |
| Cash NPAT | 9,836 | 10,252 | **+4%** | 10,982 | **+7%** |
| NIM | 1.99% | 2.08% | +9bps | 2.05% | −3bps |
| Loan loss rate (LIE/GLAA) | n/a | 0.07% | — | 0.08% | +1bp |

*Sources: CBA-FY26-profit-announcement p.16; CBA-FY25-profit-announcement p.16, p.18.*

## The rotation

FY25's cash-NPAT growth (+4%) was margin- and provision-led: NIM rose 9bps, mostly from replicating-portfolio and capital-hedge earnings (+9bps) and a liquids mix benefit (+7bps), while opex (+6%) outgrew income (+5%), holding pre-provision profit growth to +3%. The bottom line was then flattered by a shrinking impairment charge (−9%, "reflecting an improving base case economic outlook and lower loss experience").

FY26 rotates to a volume-led model. Average interest-earning assets rose 8% ($92bn), lifting NII +7% even as NIM fell 3bps to 2.05%. CBA's margin bridge (results presentation p.60) attributes the fall to Liquids & repos (−4bps) and Asset pricing (−5bps: home loan competition −3bps, cash-rate lag −1bp, business/institutional lending −1bp), partly offset by hedge income (+5bps) and Portfolio mix (+2bps, "deposits growing faster than lending"). Opex grew +6%, matching income, so pre-provision profit growth doubled to +6% and cost-to-income improved 20bps to 45.5%. Loan impairment expense rose +9% (loss rate 7bps→8bps) on "portfolio growth, cost-of-living pressures and increased geopolitical risk" — provisioning for risk, not realised losses, which the ASX announcement states "remained low," with provision coverage steady at 1.53% of credit RWA and the loss rate still below its 17-year historical range (results presentation p.69).

## Judgment

On the disclosed evidence, FY26's faster cash-NPAT growth (+7% vs +4%) is higher quality. It is broader-based (income growth matched cost growth for the first time in this comparison, doubling pre-provision profit growth to +6%) and it absorbed, rather than depended on, both NIM compression and a rising loan-loss rate — whereas FY25's growth relied on non-repeatable margin tailwinds and a shrinking impairment charge while pre-provision profit growth lagged at +3%.

## Limitations

- No published dollar bridge decomposes cash-NPAT growth into volume/margin/cost/impairment/tax; this judgment is inferred from growth-rate comparisons and the bps-level NIM bridge.
- Other operating income includes unquantified one-off items (CommInsure milestone payment, Gemini IPO gain), so "clean" organic OOI growth cannot be isolated.
- The higher loan-loss rate is expected-loss provisioning; documents assert realised losses "remained low" but disclose no write-off rate to verify this.

**Confidence: 78/100**

key_facts.fact: FY26 cash NPAT rose 7% to $10,982m (from $10,252m), a faster pace than FY25's 4% growth to $10,252m (from $9,836m).

citations.quote: Cash net profit after tax (cash NPAT or cash profit) from continuing operations increased $730 million or 7% on the prior year to $10,982 million.
Cash net profit after tax (“cash NPAT” or “cash profit”) from continuing operations increased $416 million or 4% on the prior year to $10,252 million.

key_facts.fact: The margin trend reversed: NIM rose 9bps to 2.08% in FY25 but fell 3bps to 2.05% in FY26.

citations.quote: The Bank’s net interest margin increased 9 basis points on the prior year to 2.08%.
The Bank’s net interest margin decreased by 3 basis points on the prior year to 2.05%.

key_facts.fact: FY26 loan impairment expense rose 9% to $788m and the loan loss rate ticked up 1bp to 8bps of GLAA, versus a 9% decline to $726m (loss rate 7bps) in FY25.

citations.quote: Loan impairment expense was $788 million, an increase of $62 million or 9% on the prior year.
Loan impairment expense as a percentage of average gross loans and acceptances (GLAA) increased 1 basis point to 8 basis points.
Loan impairment expense (LIE) decreased $76 million, reflecting an improving base case economic outlook and lower loss experience, partly offset by increasing geopolitical uncertainty.

key_facts.fact: Pre-provision profit growth doubled from +3% in FY25 (income +5%, opex +6%) to +6% in FY26 (income +6%, opex +6%), showing FY26 income growth caught up to cost growth.

citations.quote: The result was driven by a 3% increase in operating performance with a 5% increase in operating income and a 6% increase in operating expenses.
The result was driven by a 6% increase in operating income and a 6% increase in operating expenses 2, as well as a $62 million increase in loan impairment expense.

key_facts.fact: CBA's FY26 margin bridge attributes the 3bp NIM decline mainly to asset pricing competition (-5bps: home loan competition -3bps, cash rate lag -1bp, business/institutional lending -1bp).

citations.quote: Lower margin largely due to growth in liquids and repos – competition offset by hedge earnings
Asset pricing: Decreased margin by 5 basis points driven by home lending pricing (down 4 basis points) and business and institutional lending pricing (down 1 basis point).

key_facts.fact: The FY26 margin bridge shows hedge/replicating income continuing to offset pricing pressure: Capital, Replicating and Other added 5bps (replicating portfolio +4bps, capital hedges +1bp), similar in direction to FY25's larger 9bp tailwind from the same source.

citations.quote: Capital, Replicating and Other: Increased margin by 5 basis points driven by higher earnings on the replicating portfolio due to changes in portfolio rate and volume (up 4 basis points) and higher earnings on capital hedges (up 1 basis point).

Capital, Replicating and Other: Increased margin by 9 basis points driven by the net impact of the replicating portfolio due to changes in portfolio rate and volume (up 5 basis points) and higher earnings on capital hedges (up 4 basis points).

key_facts.fact: Growth in liquid assets and institutional repos cost the FY26 margin 4bps combined, a bridge item that did not appear in FY25 (where liquids/pooled facilities instead added 7bps).

citations.quote: Increase in liquid assets (3) Increase in institutional repos (1)

Excluding a 7 basis point increase in margin from a reduction in lower yielding liquid assets and institutional pooled facilities, which have a broadly neutral impact on net interest income, net interest margin increased 2 basis points.

key_facts.fact: FY26 net interest income grew 7% to $25,586m, driven by an 8% ($92bn) rise in average interest-earning assets that outweighed the 3bp NIM decline.

citations.quote: Net interest income was $25,586 million, an increase of $1,563 million or 7% on the prior year. The result was driven by a $92 billion or 8% increase in average interest earning assets to $1,246 billion, partly offset by a 3 basis point decrease in net interest margin to 2.05%.

key_facts.fact: FY26's higher loan-loss rate reflects provisioning for risk rather than realised losses: CBA states realised credit losses remained low and provision coverage stayed strong, with the loss rate still below its historical range.

citations.quote: loan impairment expense increased from low levels and arrears rose in some consumer portfolios, while realised credit losses remained low, overall credit quality remained sound and provision coverage remained strong
Loan impairment expense remains below historical levels

key_facts.fact: Restructuring and notable items excluded from underlying opex have risen each year ($89m FY24, $130m FY25, $170m FY26), a modest but growing drag embedded in both years' headline cost growth.

citations.quote: Relates to remediation provisions for domestic ($52 million) and NZ ($33 million) notable items as well as a Bankwest restructuring provision of $45 million in FY25 and $89 million in FY24.

FY26 relates to provisions for the settlement of legal proceedings in NZ; an additional goodwill payment made to certain customers as a result of ASIC’s Better Banking review; and domestic customer remediation.

key_facts.fact: Part of FY26's other operating income growth (+4% to $4,638m) came from non-recurring items, including a fair value gain on the Gemini IPO investment, which are not separately quantified in the disclosure.

citations.quote: Other income increased by $46 million or 42% to $156 million, mainly due to impacts from minority investments and a fair value gain on our investment in Gemini following its Initial Public Offering.

limitations: CBA does not publish a dollar-denominated bridge decomposing cash NPAT growth into volume, margin, cost, impairment and tax contributions; the FY25-vs-FY26 quality comparison here is inferred from growth-rate comparisons and the bps-level NIM bridge, not a single printed reconciliation.

Other operating income growth includes named one-off items (a CommInsure sale milestone payment, a Gemini IPO fair-value gain) that are not separately quantified in dollars in the disclosure, so the underlying organic OOI growth rate cannot be isolated from the reported +4%.

The higher FY26 loan-loss rate is driven by collective (expected-loss) provisioning; CBA states realised losses remained low but does not disclose a write-off rate in these documents to verify that claim independently.

Divisional-level margin and loan-loss detail (e.g., the per-business-unit loss-rate chart) could not be reliably read from extracted chart text/labels and was excluded from this analysis in favour of group-level figures.
